title: Date Counter
description: Count the days between two dates on a calendar, both days included, across a month end, find a finish date, and add days or a fortnight to a date.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Count the days from one date to another, counting both days, across a month end as well, find a finish date from a start date and a number of days, and find a date some days after or a fortnight later.
writeup.look: A month calendar, or two months side by side, with a run of shaded day cells, a counter that says whether both end days are included, and a violet jump of days.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Date Counter' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of days counted. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The month calendar fills the left of the area at x 90, y 230, 700 wide, in seven columns each 100 wide, with the dates in rows beneath, each row 64 tall. When a run crosses a month end, two months stand side by side, each 340 wide, with the last day of the first month marked in ink. The start date is set on it in deep blue, labelled Start, and the end date, or the number of days, beside it in deep blue, labelled Given. The days between them are shaded as a run of cells and counted one by one. The day counter stands at x 850, y 240 and says whether the first day and the last day are included. The count is green, labelled Answer, at x 850, y 560, and a last day found is green, labelled End. The Cut handle stands at x 850, y 340 and splits a run at the last day of the first month. A violet jump of days, labelled Jump, is dragged along the calendar from a date, and a jump of 14 days stands for a fortnight. The date being counted is amber. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a delete key, and keys for days and the month names. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. What the question gives, as a clock time, a length of time, a start date or a number of days, is deep blue, labelled Given or Start. What the working reaches, as an end time, a length of time, a converted time or a date, is green, labelled Answer, End or How long. The thin second hand and the seconds it counts are vermilion, labelled Second hand. One jump along a time line, and one regrouped unit carried or borrowed, are violet, labelled Jump, Carry or Regroup. On a day bar the half from noon until just before midnight is rose, labelled p.m., and the half from midnight until just before noon stays warm white inside its outline, labelled a.m. The hand, digit, column, jump or date being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. The hour hand and the minute hand, dials, tick marks, time lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last run stays shaded on the calendar with its cut, its counts by cells and by the rule, and its answer beside them in green.

writeup.delight: On the first phase, when the count by cells and the count by the rule land on the same number, the two counters flip over together and turn green at once.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet counted. On the first phase one month calendar stands with a start date and an end date set on it in deep blue and no cell shaded. On the second two months stand side by side with a start date in the first and an end date in the second. On the third a month calendar holds a start date and a number of days in deep blue. On the fourth a date is set on the calendar with a violet jump of some days waiting beside it. One thing moves, once: the start date, the first cell of the run or the jump gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any two dates set on the calendar and counted, any run cut at a month end, and any jump of days dragged from a date. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on counting both days, a run across a month end, a finish date and dates some days after.
voiceLines: A calendar with two dates marked, waiting to be counted.
Count the first day and the last day. Then take one date from the other and add one.
Where does the first month end? Count that part, then the rest.
The first day is day one. On which date does the last day fall?
After means add the days. Do you count the first day again?
A new pair of dates. Count them the same way.
Free play. Mark any two dates and count the days between.
Count the cells again. Did you count the first day and the last day?
You counted the days between dates and found a date some days after.

observations.why: the cells include both the first day and the last day, and taking one date from the other leaves one of them out.
observations.soWhat: counting both days, the number of days is the end date minus the start date, then add 1.
observations.observe: The cells counted one by one and the sum taken from the end date agreed once 1 was added.

observations.why: the two months have different numbers of days, so their dates cannot be taken apart as if they were one month.
observations.soWhat: count to the last day of the month first, then on into the next month, and add the two parts.
observations.observe: A run across a month end split into two parts at the last day of the first month.

observations.why: the first day is day 1, so it is already counted.
observations.soWhat: the last day is found by adding to the start date one day fewer than the number of days.
observations.observe: The last day of a course came one day fewer than its number of days after the first day.

observations.why: after means add the days, and the date the jump starts from is not one of them.
observations.soWhat: a fortnight later is 14 days after, and the two kinds of question, how many days and on which date, are kept apart.
observations.observe: The jump of days never counted the date it started from.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, no colour means good or bad. The miss empties the answer slot at once (every digit, every box, a picked choice), so it is empty through the traceback; the pad re-opens empty after it.
tracebacks: Phase 1: Each shaded day is counted from 1, the first day included, and end date minus start date plus 1 is written below.
Phase 2: The run is cut at the last day of the first month, each part is counted from 1, and the two parts are added.
Phase 3: The days are counted from the start date as day 1 to the last day, which turns green.
Phase 4: Jumps are counted from the day after the date, and the date the last jump lands on turns green.

voice.opening: A calendar with two dates marked, waiting to be counted.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Move the start and end dates and count the days between.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You counted the days between dates and found a date some days after.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

items.planQuestion: A book fair is open from 8 September to 16 September. For how many days is it open?

question.en: A book fair is open from 8 to 16 September; how many days, both days counted?

items.planQuestion: From 2 October to 7 October, counting both days, how many days is that?

question.en: From 2 October to 7 October, counting both days, how many days is that?

items.planQuestion: One person says a visit was after the 6th but before the 11th of a month. Another says it was after the 8th but before the 12th. If both are right, on which dates could the visit be?

question.en: Two friends say when the visit was; on which dates could it be?

items.planAnswer: The 9th and the 10th, because those are the dates after the 8th and before the 11th

items.planQuestion: A camp runs from 27 July to 8 August. For how many days does it run?

question.en: A camp runs from 27 July to 8 August; how many days, both days counted?

items.planQuestion: From 29 October to 2 November, counting both days, how many days is that?

question.en: From 29 October to 2 November, counting both days, how many days is that?

items.planAnswer: 5 days, because 3 days are in October and 2 days are in November

items.planQuestion: From 22 August to 5 September, counting both days, how many days is that?

question.en: How many days are there from 22 August to 5 September, with both days counted?

items.planAnswer: 15 days, because 10 days are in August and 5 days are in September

items.planQuestion: A 16-day course begins on 22 November. On which date does it end?

question.en: A 16-day course begins on 22 November; on which date does it end?

items.planQuestion: A 6-day fair begins on 10 October. On which date does it end?

question.en: A fair of 6 days starts on 10 October; what is its last day?

items.planAnswer: 15 October, because 5 days after 10 October is 15 October

items.planQuestion: A 40-day course ended on 10 August. On which date did it begin, counting both days?

question.en: A 40-day course ended on 10 August; when did it begin, both days counted?

items.planAnswer: 2 July, because 39 days before 10 August is 2 July

items.planQuestion: A plant is watered on 12 April and again 25 days after. On which date is it watered the second time?

question.en: A plant is watered on 12 April and again 25 days after; on which date is that?

items.planQuestion: What date is 10 days after 6 October?

question.en: What date is 10 days after 6 October?

items.planQuestion: A jar is filled on 27 October and opened a fortnight later. On which date is it opened?

question.en: A jar is filled on 27 October and opened a fortnight later; which date?

items.planAnswer: 10 November, because 14 days after 27 October is 10 November

scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.
